chunks: If you raise your hand to kill me, I will raise not mine to kill you, for I fear God, the Lord of all the worlds;
ai.seo_question: What did Hudh say to Qarun when he proposed killing him?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to illustrate the superiority of the righteous brother (Hudh/Abel) over the arrogant aggressor (Qarun/Cain), emphasizing that true victory lies in steadfastness rather than retaliation. It underscores the principle of *taqwa* (God-consciousness) as the ultimate deterrent against sin, even when one has the power to strike back. This narrative serves as a foundational model for ethical conduct in familial and social conflicts, highlighting patience (*sabr*) as a divine virtue.
